spec_match.rationale: Implements the explainer's developer usage example verbatim: showNotification with data, notificationclick → matchAll → client.focus() → postMessage({delegate:'popup'}), synchronous window.open in the page's message handler, the openWindow no-client fallback, and the control/expiry/double arms mapping to the explainer's three key execution scenarios.

interactive.rationale: Real permission request, real notification, four selectable experiment arms, a six-step live status board, and an opener-connected popup that synchronously reads in-memory state from this tab.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises the end-to-end flow with honest popup-blocked outcomes and the three edge toggles; all present.

edge_cases.rationale: Permission denied is an explicit honest dead end; the worker reports focus() and delegate-call errors verbatim and falls back to a plain message; the page distinguishes 'delegate call did not throw' from 'a token actually arrived' (decided only by the real window.open result); popup-allowlist environments are called out in the logs.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5091965583622144, the explainer usage example and the Chrome sample.

conformance.rationale: Is the named observation route for three manual suite assertions (delegated open, 1s expiry, single-use invariant); its arms perform exactly those real calls.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless verification went as far as a headless environment can: in headless-shell both viewports rendered with 0px overflow, worker registered, and the permission-denied dead end displayed honestly (no fake showNotification); in full Chromium 141 with notifications granted, showNotification genuinely resolved and the lab advanced to 'click the notification'. Stages 4–6 require a human click on an OS notification, which headless cannot produce — they are verified to report their waiting state honestly, not verified complete.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts registration, permission outcome, notification shown/failed, each arm's open attempt with arm+outcome detail, and the popup's opener round-trip.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only (popup-target included); step states pair colour with the literal words done/failed/waiting; buttons pair background and color.

accessibility.rationale: Steps are an ordered list with textual states, the log is a role=log live region, arms are a fieldset/legend radio group, buttons are labelled by visible text, focus-visible outlines throughout.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Both classes driven: 0px overflow, stacked steps and arms, 44px controls. (Notification UX itself is the OS's; the page stays usable on both classes.)

openQuestions.title: Complete stages 4-6 interactively on a flagged build and on stable
openQuestions.detail: A human run is needed for the notification click. On a CapabilityDelegationPopup build (--enable-experimental-web-platform-features): delegate arm should open the popup without page activation, expiry arm should block after 1.5s, double arm should open exactly one. On released Chrome: all arms should hit the popup blocker (the gap the feature closes). Record both runs' step boards and the popup's opener/shared-state readout.

openQuestions.title: Headless-shell reports Notification.permission as denied despite a granted context permission
openQuestions.detail: Playwright's notifications permission grant produced granted in full Chromium but denied in the headless shell. Harmless for visitors (the page handles both honestly), but worth knowing for future automated runs: use the full chrome binary when exercising stage 3.

guidanceConsulted.query: multi step flow status announcement focus transitions
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Make multi-stage async flows legible: textual per-step state plus a single announced log; predictable focus transitions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Six-step board with literal state words, role=log for outcomes; the focus()-then-open ordering follows the explainer's predictable-focus rationale, quoted in the copy.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer in-flow, persistent status surfaces over transient overlays for state users must not miss.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Statuses are persistent in-flow list items and a log, not toasts — the flow spans an OS notification interaction where a transient overlay would be missed.

guidanceConsulted.query: popup amplification notification click one gesture
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: One user gesture must never yield multiple popups or ambient capabilities.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The double-open and expiry arms exist to demonstrate exactly those bounds, with honest logging either way.

summary: The explainer's webmail scenario as a working lab: real worker, real notification, real delegation attempt, real popup with synchronous opener state-sharing, and arms for the control, expiry and single-use scenarios. Headless verification covered registration, permission paths, a genuinely shown notification (full Chromium) and both viewport classes; the human-click stages honestly display their waiting state and are the recorded open question.
